headline: Trump pardoned two turkeys. They weigh 82 pounds.
summary: Freedom and Feathers, two four-month-old turkeys from a West Virginia farm, got a "complete and total pardon" on the White House South Lawn on Tuesday. They retire to Texas A&M. The ceremony is the 79th; the pardon itself dates to George H. W. Bush in 1989. Trump used his speech to talk up his new ballroom and complain about the election.

cover_question.q: Why does a turkey get a pardon?

cover_answer: A photo-op. Presidents have done it since 1989.
table_question: If you could pardon one thing you did this year, what would it be?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: Two turkeys named Freedom and Feathers went to the White House yesterday, and the president said nobody gets to eat them. Together they weigh 82 pounds, about as much as a big dog. Now they go to live at a college in Texas. Grown-ups play this joke every year before Thanksgiving, and the turkeys get the good end of it.
5-7.why: Two birds, one rule, a happy ending. That is the whole story at this age.
5-7.why_long: A seven-year-old takes one vivid feature for the whole event, so the script gives them the one that matters: two named turkeys that nobody gets to eat. The 82 pounds and the big dog put the birds at a size they can picture. Expect 'can we pardon ours?' No. Ours is already in the fridge, and that is how Thanksgiving works.

8-12.script: A pardon is the president wiping out someone's punishment. Since 1989, presidents have given one to a turkey each Thanksgiving, for fun. This year's two were picked in an online poll and will retire at Texas A&M. A tradition works like field day: it repeats, so nobody has to decide it again.
8-12.why: Poll, pardon, retirement. Field day is the mechanism.
8-12.why_long: A twelve-year-old is working out rules and who gets to apply them, and here is a real legal power used on a bird. The script hands over the chain, poll to lawn to Texas A&M, and field day as the mechanism for why a joke keeps happening. Expect 'can he pardon anyone?' People, yes, for federal crimes. That part is not a joke.

13-17.script: Why does a president pardon a turkey? The turkey industry has sent one since 1947, and Bush made it a pardon in 1989. Trump used Tuesday's to praise his new ballroom and complain about the election. Second: PETA says the pardoned birds usually die young anyway. Does that spoil the joke?
13-17.why: Two true things: a harmless tradition, and a stage a president uses as he likes.
13-17.why_long: A fifteen-year-old can hold two true things at once: a harmless 79-year-old tradition, and a president using its microphone for a ballroom and an election grievance. The script gives them the dates and PETA's line, then asks whether the joke survives. Expect 'why is this even news?' Fair question. The answer is the cameras.

5-7.q: Did the turkeys do something bad?
5-7.a: No. It's a pretend pardon. They are two lucky turkeys who don't get cooked.

8-12.a: An online poll last week. A West Virginia farm raised them.
They retire to Texas A&M. Freedom likes Dr Pepper.

13-17.q: Why does a turkey get a pardon?
13-17.a: Nobody has to. Bush made the photo-op a tradition in 1989.

13-17.q: Why give a political speech at a turkey event?
13-17.a: The cameras are there. Biden used it for a ballot joke in 2022.
